headline: Seasonal Parking Permits and Peak Summer Lodging Deadlines
reservation: Access to local beaches like Goose Rocks requires a specific parking permit during the summer months, available through the town office; this is separate from hotel parking. The famous Christmas Prelude and summer weekends often book out a year in advance, so verify individual restaurant and inn policies directly with the providers.

days.title: Historic Village and River Views

stops.name: Dock Square
stops.detail: Walk the historic center to see the 19th-century architecture and the bridge spanning the Kennebunk River.

stops.name: Grist Mill Pond
stops.detail: View the scenic tidal pond and the historic buildings that reflect the town's maritime and milling history.

days.driving: Minimal; local walking within the village center
days.note: Sidewalks are narrow and can be crowded during summer weekends; morning walks offer the best photo opportunities.

days.title: Rugged Coastline and Architecture

stops.name: Ocean Avenue
stops.detail: Drive or bike this scenic route to see the rocky Maine coastline and the historic summer 'cottages'.

stops.name: Walker’s Point
stops.detail: View the prominent peninsula that has served as a summer retreat for the Bush family for generations.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for a slow loop with stops; conditions vary
days.note: Ocean Avenue has limited stopping points; use designated pullouts to enjoy the views without obstructing traffic.

days.title: Coastal Conservation and Beaches
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from Goose Rocks Beach

stops.name: Goose Rocks Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy a walk on the soft sands of this protected barrier beach, ensuring you have the required town permit.

stops.name: Rachel Carson National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Walk the marshland trails to observe local bird species and the unique salt marsh ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes from the village to the beach areas
days.note: Beach parking is strictly enforced; check the town's official website for current permit kiosk locations.

intel.title: Village Center Limits
intel.text: Public parking in Dock Square is limited to short-term stays and fills quickly by noon. Utilize the peripheral lots or walk from your inn to avoid the midday search for a space.

intel.title: Reliable Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is generally excellent throughout the village and along Ocean Avenue. Expect minor signal drops only in the deeper wooded sections of the Wildlife Refuge.

intel.title: Route 1 Conveniences
intel.text: Most fuel and grocery services are located along the Route 1 corridor in neighboring Kennebunk. The village center is primarily boutique shops and restaurants with fewer utilitarian services.

intel.title: Tidal Changes
intel.text: The Kennebunk River is tidal; boat departures and even some low-lying paths are affected by the twice-daily cycles. Check local tide charts if you plan to explore the riverbanks.

intel.title: Beach Permit Rules
intel.text: Goose Rocks Beach requires a parking sticker from June through Labor Day. These are non-transferable and must be displayed according to town ordinances to avoid fines.

plan.arrival: Fly into Portland International Jetport (PWM), rent a car, and drive 30 minutes south to Kennebunkport, checking in at your inn before heading to Dock Square.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is ideal; larger RVs are not recommended for the narrow, winding streets of the historic district or the limited parking at Walker's Point.
plan.goldenHour: St. Ann's Episcopal Church on the coast offers a view of the Atlantic horizon, though access is subject to parish events.
